excerpt: Indianapolis Colts won 19-17. The number landed, and some of the reasoning behind it held up. Take the result; do not take it as confirmation of the parts that did not.
seo_description: Indianapolis Colts beat Houston Texans 19-17. EdgeDesk’s number implied Indianapolis Colts +2.5 — win. 2 of 11 gradeable claims held up, 2 did not. Process grade: MIXED. Research, not picks.
model_status_note: The number landed, and some of the reasoning behind it held up. Take the result; do not take it as confirmation of the parts that did not.

tally.headline: 2 of 11 gradeable claims held up, 2 did not

implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 4.3 points toward Indianapolis Colts of the quote EdgeDesk captured at FanDuel. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk’s fair total of 44.8 sat 1.3 points above the captured total of 43.5.

closing_line.note: The line moved 1 points toward the side EdgeDesk’s number leaned before kickoff. That is the market arriving where EdgeDesk already was, and over many games it is the only evidence that a disagreement carried information.

reasons: 0 claims held up, 7 held up in direction only and 2 did not. Parts of the read were right and parts were not.
The result carries 1 high-variance marker — a 3-turnover swing — so the scoreboard is weaker evidence than it looks.
EdgeDesk projected a home margin of 1.8 and the game finished 2 the home way — 0.2 points of margin error, inside the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

variance_markers.label: A 3-turnover swing
variance_markers.text: Houston Texans won the turnover battle by 3. Turnover margin is the least repeatable thing in football: it moves scoreboards hard and predicts almost nothing about the next meeting, so a result built on it says less about either team than the scoreline suggests.

variance_markers.label: A 2-point game
variance_markers.text: A game this close is decided inside the noise of any projection. Whichever way it fell, it is weak evidence about either team.

verdict.line: The number landed, and some of the reasoning behind it held up. Take the result; do not take it as confirmation of the parts that did not.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named Houston Texans as better in passing and the game went the other way, across 2 separate published claims. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: every signal this claim rests on went the other way
lessons.suggested_investigation: These claims carried 4.1 points of the published number between them and were contradicted. Check whether the same category has been contradicted in other games this season before touching anything.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 2 of the claims in this article rested on model, matchup.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver; no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes Points allowed.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model, matchup.
